findings.description: The loop compares len(self._keys_by_country), the number of distinct countries, with max_entries. The cache therefore only evicts once there are more countries than max_entries, so it can hold unlimited entries per country, and the limit is effectively never enforced. Memory grows without bound as new postal codes are seen, within the TTL. The `evictions` metric will also stay at 0.
findings.title: Eviction bound checks number of countries instead of number of entries

findings.description: clear() drops entries without counting them as evictions or invalidations. Stats remain consistent only loosely, which may mislead metrics. This is minor.
findings.title: clear() does not reset or account for stats

findings.description: When an expired entry is reloaded, the key is re-added to the set, which is fine. However, if the loader raises (UnknownJurisdiction), the stale expired entry stays in the cache and counts toward size. It is also still counted as a miss. Expired entries are never purged except by LRU, so they occupy slots.
findings.suggestion: Delete the expired entry (and its index entry) before calling the loader.
findings.title: Expired entry replaced without cleaning country index consistency
